title: GeoGPT: AI-driven Marine Ecosystem Monitoring and Protection
summary: Zhejiang Lab reports that its GeoGPT platform identifies deep-sea species with 81.3% accuracy and takes 40 milliseconds per image, compared with 40 seconds manually.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: In its submission to the International Telecommunication Union, current as of June 2025, Zhejiang Lab describes GeoGPT as a research and product platform for geoscience analysis. The lab reports that GeoGPT identifies deep-sea species with 81.3% accuracy. It also reports that recognition time fell from 40 seconds to 40 milliseconds per image. The intended applications include marine monitoring and less disruptive exploration. The marine figures rest on the makers' submission alone. No source establishes that ecosystem losses were avoided. Cleverley and colleagues reported on 25 July 2026 that the International Union of Geological Sciences had suspended Deep-time Digital Earth, the program behind GeoGPT, in early 2025. They also reported that core GeoGPT software remains proprietary.
purpose: Accelerate geoscience information processing and support marine decisions.

ratings.reason: Zhejiang Lab reports that image recognition takes 40 milliseconds, compared with 40 seconds manually. No source establishes an ecological outcome.
Reduced mining damage and avoided algal disasters are intended outcomes, and no source reports that either occurred.

ai_role.statement: The account does not isolate AI’s contribution from the surrounding workflow.

evidence.citation: Paul H. Cleverley, Ezzoura Errami, Tania R. Marshall, Simon Burnett, Andrew Osarumwense Lator and Ibeke Ebuka, Open at the interface, closed at the core: neutrality claims in AI-enabled geoscience infrastructure focusing on Africa - The case of Deep-Time Digital Earth and GeoGPT, Journal of Geoethics and Social Geosciences, 25 July 2026. The authors work at universities and firms in the United Kingdom, Morocco, South Africa and Nigeria with no role in GeoGPT, and two of them hold or held posts in bodies of the International Union of Geological Sciences; they report that the union suspended the program behind GeoGPT and that core GeoGPT software remains proprietary, and they do not test the marine tools.
